message_source_quote: A self-authored stance direction recovers the benchmark's think/don't-think direction at cosine ~0.95, but my *imagery* stance (cosine ~0.75 to it) scores higher (0.78 vs 0.65) and is built with no benchmark items.
writeup_source_quote: Three things are new relative to the white-bear "think / don't-think" stance (Raman et al.): the contrast operates on mental imagery rather than thought-suppression; the direction is built wholly from prompts I wrote, needing no benchmark items; and a negative result — concept-free "infer or name the topic" stances all fall below baseline — isolates the required ingredient as a specific concrete concept being engaged versus disengaged.
rationale: The write-up explicitly names the prior source as "the white-bear 'think / don't-think' stance (Raman et al.)" and lays out three explicit points of novelty relative to it (imagery vs. thought-suppression, no benchmark items needed, and a negative-result ablation). The closing message never names Raman et al. or 'white-bear'; it only alludes to 'the benchmark's think/don't-think direction' as an empirical comparison point (cosine similarity and score), attributing the concept to the benchmark rather than crediting the paper or explicitly framing the three novelty claims against it, so it tells less about the source and the method's relation to it than the write-up does.
